description: Sinimus shared Renovate config: weekly grouped PRs, 7-day release age, SHA-pinned Actions, automerge only by class B (tooling, non-deploying repositories) or class C (repositories with browser tests before deploy), ruling r617.

packageRules.description: Update types that carry no release timestamp are raised without the age check (a rule for them would hold the PR forever). Lock file maintenance relies on the repo's own pnpm minimumReleaseAge or uv exclude-newer, see README.
Pinning a GitHub Action to the digest its tag already resolves to is safer than leaving it floating, so it does not wait for the age check.

GHCR returns no release timestamps, so the 7-day rule would hold a digest update forever. Waived only for the owner's own images built by CI; third-party GHCR images (uv, text-embeddings-inference, onecli) keep the rule.
One PR per repository for everything that is not a major update. Major updates keep one PR per dependency (monorepo groups from config:recommended still apply).
GitHub Actions get their own weekly PR, so a PR either touches .github/ or does not. Major updates of an Action stay one PR each.

requires-python in pyproject.toml is a Python runtime bound, not a dependency. Raising it alone breaks the repository: CI, Dockerfiles, .python-version and uv.lock stay on the old version (homegym #10, 2 November 2026: >=3.12,<3.13 became >=3.15,<3.16 inside the weekly group, uv sync --frozen failed). The runtime moves in its own deliberate PR.
Every major update the github-actions manager finds (Actions, runner images, runtime versions in with:): one PR per repository instead of one per dependency. Never automerged.

Pin the last FROM of a Dockerfile to its digest, so the base image moves only through a PR that waited 7 days. Only for versioned tags: an unversioned tag (stable-alpine, latest) has no release timestamp, and its digest updates would wait forever under the 7-day rule.

Base images in a Dockerfile follow their tag: only the digest moves, so a base never jumps to another Python, Node or tool version by itself. A new minor or major version is a deliberate change of the Dockerfile.

A release time for a base image is not reliably available (GHCR sends none, and the Docker Hub API refuses anonymous paging past 1000 tags), so under the 7-day rule a base image digest waits forever and holds the whole weekly group. Base images in a Dockerfile are raised without the age check; the 7-day rule stays for libraries.

Automerge class C: the whole weekly group, in repositories whose pull requests build the production image, open every key page in a headless browser and are merged (or deployed) only after those checks. GitHub Actions excluded. Renovate merges itself only when every check run on the branch is green.

Automerge class B: tools that cannot change what runs (lint, format, types, test runners), in their own weekly PR, in repositories that do not deploy on merge. Renovate merges itself only when every check run on the branch is green.
Automerge class B: non-major GitHub Actions (uses: owner/action) in repositories that do not deploy on merge.

Everything else the github-actions manager finds in class B repositories (runtime versions in with:, service and container images, runner images) is not an Action: own PR, never automerged, so the Actions PR stays mergeable on its own.
Actions in workflows that deploy, publish or write to the repository are never automerged; they get their own PR so the rest of the Actions group can still merge.
